followup_reviews.Research finding: The Bridge I passenger/private-car interruption and January 2023 reopening are supported; retain inclusion and bounded operational duration. Bridge I is distinct from Bridge II freight. Returnee diversions, driver/conductor exceptions, border-pass and health conditions are retained; no whole-frontier shutdown is inferred. Contemporaneous accounts give 21 and 22 March 2020; the later government news account gives 23 March. Retain 21–23 March onset to observed 12 January 2023 reopening, 1025–1027 calendar days, with qualified continuity. Human disease control is the attributed initial purpose. Security / Unspecified security remains explicitly analytical context for later continuation, as reflected in official Thai tourism reporting; it is not recast as a sole official rationale. All four decisive current source bodies were directly inspected. A historical alternative MDN URL failed and supplies no new claim. Similar government news republication does not multiply independent evidence. The phase remains unlocated. Bridge identity and scope are checked but this audit does not author or approve coordinates.

Accept the baseline challenger’s source-language, goods-attribution and Greek article-number refinements plus the additional limited source readings. The eight new parents require no further factual changes: preserve their cohort, policy/schedule, day-level, unknown-endpoint and location qualifications. This is a completed audit procedure for the sample, not proof every attribute or every record in the register is verified.
